title: Unit Testing in Rust
goal: Write unit tests using the test attribute and test modules.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Unit Tests

sections.text: You write unit tests as regular functions marked with the `#[test]` attribute. You do not need an external test framework library to get started.

sections.caption: The #[test] attribute turns a function into a test runner target.

sections.text: Unit tests usually live in a nested module named `tests`. Annotating that module with `#[cfg(test)]` ensures test code is excluded from production builds.
In Rust, nested modules do not inherit parent scope items automatically. You must bring items from the outer module into scope using `use super::*;`.

sections.caption: use super::*; imports outer module functions into the test scope.

sections.text: Omitting `use super::*;` causes compiler error `E0425` when calling functions defined in the parent module.

explanation: Write unit tests using the test attribute and test modules.
